items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: So I walked up to him and I told him, and I must have said it in a gangster-like way or something.

ctx.x: Yeah. Did you know Bix well?

Yeah, I knew Bix pretty well. Like I tell you, Moore threw that. And then he came down a couple of times when he was with Whiteman. He and Frank Trombauer were with Whiteman. We like broke the thing up. They did a concert, you see. And there was no jazz at all. So after the intermission, we were in the alley side. It was old St. Charles said up there. They've torn it down now, I think. Well, I was delegated to go up and speak to Whiteman and tell him that we wanted to hear some Bix and Tram, you see. So I walked…
You had to coerce Whiteman to get any jazz.

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: Well, Paul came up and he complimented me on the horn, you see.

ctx.x: But what about Snoozer? You were going to tell about how?

Well, yeah. While they were here, while Whiteman was here, Snoozer was in town. So Brownlee and I, we wanted Whiteman to hear Snoozer, you see. And I had known Whiteman from Tony Perentich, man. I was working at the halfway house with Abby and I was just learning how to play a cornet thing, you see. And I think I knew about four or five tunes. And Abby used to say, you never learn how to play a thing as long as you live. And I told him, I'll see the day when I was stuck like that, you know. And they used to…
Not that one, but some of the others.
